annotation.title_clean: Ethical Design in Medical AI Robotics: Between Innovation and Responsibility
annotation.title_en: Ethical Design in Medical AI Robotics: Between Innovation and Responsibility
named_instruments_referenced: EU Ethics by Design and Ethics of Use Approaches for AI
EU Ethics Guidelines for Trustworthy AI
annotation.summary_en: Romanian conceptual journal article on 'ethics by design' for AI-powered medical and surgical robots. It reviews EU ethics guidance and the literature on robotic surgery, and identifies dilemmas around transparency, privacy, accountability and meaningful human control. It proposes a model that builds ethics into the design process and calls for enforceable regulation and unified standards.
key_provisions_or_claims: Ethics must be built into medical robot design from the concept stage, not added afterwards
Medical AI robots require meaningful human control and an active human physician (e.g., in telesurgery)
Traceability and explainability mechanisms are needed for patient safety and legal liability
Calls for proactive, enforceable regulation and unified standards for autonomous surgical robots
Identifies the 'moral crumple zone' risk, where blame falls on surgeons even when the system acted autonomously
